what_worked: AI's total revenue dominance is correctly identified and the Cursor case study is engaging.
fix_next: Most slides abandon the TrustMRR dataset for external stats; fabricated category revenues (SaaS $1420K, Mobile Apps $980K) undermine credibility.
verdict: External hype piece with fabricated dataset figures, not a data story.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: SaaS revenue shown as $1420K (actual $703K); Mobile Apps $980K (actual $228K); Productivity $720K (actual $114K); Marketing $610K (actual $1317K); Dev Tools $540K (actual $163K); Health $390K (actual $179K); Education $310K (actual $524K). The '1.7x more than #2 SaaS' claim is wrong—#2 is Marketing at $1.32M. The entire bar chart appears fabricated.

evidence.insight: Slide 2 makes the obvious observation that AI has highest total revenue but never examines median revenue, per-company efficiency, or why AI leads (volume vs. quality). No analysis of missingness, payment providers, anonymity, or any other dataset dimension. Slides 3-7 are entirely external research about Cursor and the AI market—not dataset insights.
evidence.narrative: The thesis 'AI is dominant' is stated on slide 1 and repeated on slide 8, but the middle is split between one dataset slide (slide 2) and four slides of external Cursor/market research. The DAU/MAU analysis (slide 4) uses no TrustMRR data at all. No synthesis between dataset findings and external claims.
evidence.framing: No discussion of dataset limitations: 274 missing categories, 241 missing countries, 216 zero-revenue companies. No acknowledgment that AI's total revenue lead is partly a volume effect (197 companies vs. smaller categories). Audience and analytical question are never explicitly stated. '29 categories' is stated but the dataset reference shows 12 named categories with 274 missing.
evidence.accuracy: Slide 2 bar chart has at least 6 materially wrong revenue figures. The ranking is wrong (#2 should be Marketing, not SaaS). No mention of median revenue where AI ($503) ranks far below Education ($2,435) and Marketing ($2,370). External claims on slides 3-7 are unverifiable from the dataset and unsourced inline.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark theme with good color hierarchy and readable typography. Cards and bar charts are clean. However, the visual polish masks fabricated data. Slides 5-7 are essentially marketing collateral for Cursor, not analytical visuals.
evidence.ai_slop: Slides 3 and 7 read like AI-generated consulting filler ('Product-Led Flywheel,' 'Massive TAM,' 'Capital Efficiency,' 'The $540B Opportunity'). The entire Cursor deep-dive (slides 5-7) could appear in any AI hype deck regardless of dataset. Generic three-column frameworks on slide 7.
